summary: Fix makes comma-splitting bracket-aware so regexes with commas inside `(){}[]` (e.g. `(foo{1,3})`) survive parsing, resolving the reported crash. But it hand-rolls a fragile bracket counter and drops the whitespace-stripping that `_csv_transformer` previously applied, changing behavior for existing `a, b` style configs.

issues.description: Old path used `_csv_transformer`, which strips whitespace around each token. New per-char parser does NOT strip, so `bad-name-rgxs = foo, bar` now yields regex ` bar` with a literal leading space — silent behavioral regression for the common comma+space config style.

Manual bracket-depth counter is brittle: treats `()`, `[]`, `{}` interchangeably (mismatched pairs like `(a]` still balance to 0), ignores regex escaping (`\(` / `\)` are literals but still increment/decrement depth), and doesn't account for char-class semantics where `(`/`{` shouldn't count. Handles the reported case but not general regex grammar.
No comment explaining the bracket-tracking logic or why commas inside brackets are not split; non-obvious to future maintainers.
